title: Banigoba — App Review Checklist
meeting: App review meeting, 14 October 2026 (full transcript, parts 1–3)
status: Splash, turn-around and feed cards built on 26 Oct, not yet seen on a phone. Today: phone check, then the feed server job and content engine.
target: Next app version by the end of next week (about Friday 23 October 2026)

tiers.name: Principles (apply to all work)
tiers.blurb: Not tasks. Keep these in mind on every change.

items.text: Copy the basics from WhatsApp, X and Instagram. Do not reinvent standard patterns; add our own ideas on top later.
Make the app habit-forming: people should want to check it every 15 minutes. User numbers will grow slowly, so engagement matters.
The backend engine and its algorithms are the top priority. That is where the app's power comes from.

tiers.name: Tier 1 — Quick wins
tiers.blurb: Small, clear UI changes, or checks of work that is already done. Start here.

tiers.name: Tier 2 — Clear, medium work
tiers.blurb: The requirement is clear. These need more than a one-line change.

items.text: Every page has a clear heading at the top. Move the top bar up and put the page title in it.
items.progress: Wardrobe heading is "My Smart Wardrobe"; the Discover tab heading now matches the bottom bar; Home's tabs name each feed.

items.text: Fix text that overlaps or clashes, on every screen.
items.progress: Fixed where found (makeover method labels, profile photo tiles). Still needs a check on a real phone.

items.text: Make the layout a clear either-or: Option A, describe the look; or Option B, use a look you love (style idol, style twin, community).
items.progress: Two large choices: "Describe it" or "Use a look you love". The second shows Style twin, Style idol, Trending and Weather.

items.text: Option A: the "Describe the look you want" box sits at the top, with the "What should change" chips (hair, outfit, shoes and so on) below it.
items.progress: The description box sits under "How do you want to create your look?", with "What should change?" below it.

items.text: The user must write a description AND pick at least one change chip before Generate is enabled. These chips label our backend data sets.
items.progress: Nothing is pre-selected. Generate stays off until there is a description (or a chosen look) and a "What should change" choice.

items.text: The chips are generic. They do not try to adapt to what is in the uploaded photo.
items.progress: The chips are the same for every photo: Full look, Outfit only, Hair only, Top only, Bottom only.

items.text: Option B also asks the user what should change (outfit only, hair, and so on).
items.progress: The same "What should change?" chips apply to a look you love.

items.text: If the Smart Wardrobe is not set up, show "Set up your Smart Wardrobe" with a button that opens the setup.
items.progress: An empty feed shows "Set up my Smart Wardrobe" and "Add my measurements" buttons.

items.text: Friends' shared daily dress-ups also appear here, not only yours.
items.progress: Forward a dress-up to Friends or Community to share it as today's look. Friends' shared dress-ups from the last 36 hours show at the top of the feed.

items.text: The feed shows everyone's looks (yours, friends, followers, community and public), not only yours. People want engagement.
items.progress: My Fashion Makeover shows your looks plus everyone else's you are allowed to see. Community shows only other people's.

items.text: After saving, show a sheet that says where the look went and lets the user pick or create a category. Today it just says "Saved", which feels like a dark hole.
items.progress: After saving, a sheet says "Saved to My Smart Wardrobe", offers categories (or a new one) and a "View in wardrobe" button.

items.text: The Smart Wardrobe page currently shows the wrong content (friends and community). Give it its own wardrobe interface.
items.progress: Tabs are now My Clothes, Saved Looks (grouped by category) and Shops & Designers. The Friends and Community tabs are gone. My Clothes stays empty until the user_products rule (issue I-1) is deployed.

items.text: Add item: add size fields (size, shoulders and other key measurements).
items.progress: Add item asks for size (XXS–XXXL), shoulders and length. These are stored in the same fields shops use. Uploading only works once the user_products rule (issue I-1) is deployed.

items.text: Add search for people and friends.
items.progress: Search was on Discover; there is now a search icon on Home and a "Find people to follow" button on your profile. Search no longer shows emails and matches an email only when the full address is typed. Your email is shown only to you.

items.text: The Community feed includes events.
items.progress: An "Upcoming events" strip sits at the top of the Community feed.

items.text: Add a "Create event" entry point and form (for example to announce a fashion show) that posts into Community.
items.progress: There is an "Add event" button on the Community feed. It uses the existing event form, which goes to curators for approval.

items.text: Moderate free-text comments the way affirmations are moderated (harassment, body shaming, spam), with encouraging wording in the interface.
items.progress: Not started. Affirmations are moderated; comments are not.
items.note: From the client's product-design document (4 Nov 2026)

tiers.name: Tier 3 — Needs a decision first
tiers.blurb: Blocked on an open question at the end of this document. Quick to build once decided.

items.text: Change the payoff line (tagline) to "g, for "Looking Good!!!"", as in the designer's animation.
items.progress: 27 Oct: updated to the designer's final video. The line is now exactly for, "Looking Good!!!" in bold, beside the g, sized and spaced as in the video; it types in letter by letter with a soft fade on the newest letters. The sound is now the designer's new sound logo (about 4 s, about 60 KB, made louder so it is easy to hear, with a short fade in and out), lined up so the g appears on its first accent. The splash is held about 3.8 s, instead of the video's 7.8 s. Reduced-motion phones see the finished line at once. Waiting on: a check on a real phone (the phone was not reachable, so I only checked rendered frames against the video), and the designer's font file if you want the text to match the video exactly (the app uses its own bold font, which looks very close)

items.text: Remove the "No affirmations yet" text. Show a number instead.
items.note: Open question 1: this clashes with the work plan's "no counters" rule
items.progress: Decided: owner-only count. "No affirmations yet" is gone. The look's owner sees the total; everyone else sees which affirmations were given, never a number (fits BNG SRS 001).

items.text: Add a way to follow people. "Following" and "Followers" appear on the profile, but nothing lets you follow anyone.
items.progress: Follow already existed on other people's profiles and is now reachable through people search. Follower and following numbers show only to the profile owner; others see the lists without totals.

items.text: Make Post and Share clearly different, or merge them. Remove the duplication and settle the wording.
items.progress: Decided: keep both, renamed. "Post" (in the ⋮ menu) decides who sees the look in the feeds; "Send to" (share icon) sends it to a salon, shop, designer, WhatsApp or other apps. Community and Friends are no longer in Send to. Daily Dress Up has its own "Post as today's dress-up" action.

items.text: Repost and Quote are always visible in the share sheet. Today they only appear after you share to Community.
items.note: Today quoting is only possible on public looks. Open question 3.
items.progress: Decided: always shown. On a private look, Repost or Quote first asks "Share this look first?", then carries on.

items.text: Starting a makeover offers two choices: "Hairstyle" and "Other" (outfit, shoes, accessories). People think about their hair and face every morning more than about their full outfit.
items.note: Open question 6: two buttons or one button that asks
items.progress: Decided: one button, then a choice. "Create My Fashion Makeover" (and the menu item) asks Hairstyle or Outfit & more first.

items.text: New feature: users connect with their own salons, shops and designers. We need a name for this kind of connection.
items.progress: Decided: "My Circle". Add or remove any salon, shop or designer from the Send to list; kept privately per user.

items.text: Share to salon, shop or designer: show a row of the ones you are already connected to above the search box.
items.progress: Send to shows your Circle as a one-tap row above the search, then everyone else.

items.text: Platform commission on every sale, like InDrive (for example $1.00 item + $0.20).
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version, in the database): the buyer pays the seller's price plus 20% (a $1.00 piece costs $1.20); the seller's own price is untouched. The checkout shows "Service fee" as its own line, and the rate sits in one settings row curators can change. The database works the numbers out when the order is placed. Buyers pay the shop directly, so the shop owes Banigoba the commission: Earnings (in provider mode) shows it as due once an order is collected or delivered, pending while open, settled once paid. Needs the new migration deployed (supabase db push). Not yet on a phone.

items.text: Influencers share in the revenue from sales they bring in.
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version, backend only): when an order carries a referrer, that person is owed 25% of the commission (5c on a $1.00 piece), recorded in the ledger and shown on their Earnings screen. The database ignores a referrer who is the buyer or the shop. Still missing: the app does not yet record who brought a sale, because there is no screen where a shopper buys from someone's post or link. Decide how an influencer's link or post leads to a purchase, then pass its owner into the bag.

items.text: Buy online with delivery, so people do not have to queue or walk around a crowded flea market.
items.progress: Built 29 Oct (first version): a shop sets, in My Shop > Delivery, whether it delivers itself, the delivery fee (or free), the areas it covers (empty means anywhere the buyer gives an address) and a note. At checkout the buyer chooses \"Collect from the shop\" (pay upon collection) or \"Deliver to me\" (pay on delivery), picks an area from the shop's list, and sees items + delivery fee = total. The fee is recomputed from the shop's saved settings when the order is placed, so the app cannot set the price; delivery needs the buyer's own street address (a collection point does not count). Orders keep how they are fulfilled, the fee and the area. The seller's Orders screen shows \"Deliver to Avondale · \$3.00\" or \"Customer collects\" and offers the steps that fit: collection ends Ready for collection > Collected, delivery ends Out for delivery > Delivered; the buyer is told at each step (chat message and notification), and the provider inbox marks delivery orders. Not yet: tried on a real phone; a buyer-side \"My orders\" screen (buyers follow status through notifications and the shop chat); delivery tracking beyond status (no map, no driver); payment is still cash on collection or delivery.

items.text: Fashion-content engine: search the internet and the fashion industry for stories and post them to users' feeds, asking "What do you think about this look?" Examples: what is happening in Paris, what Michelle Obama wore 10 days ago, what local Harare socialites are wearing. This works before we have many users.
items.progress: Decided 22 Oct: show a credited link preview (title, small image and site name from the source) that opens the source; never copy images to our servers. Not built yet. Planned 25 Oct: see docs/plans/service-provider-mode.md (shopping phases). | Built 28 Oct (first version): a scheduled job (every 3 hours) reads 14 publishers' own RSS/Atom feeds (Vogue, Fashionista, ELLE, Harper's Bazaar, The Guardian, Fashion Week Online, BellaNaija, and Zimbabwean news sites such as The Herald, NewZimbabwe, ZBC, 263Chat), keeps the fashion stories, and stores each as a credited link preview: title, a link to the source's own picture, the source's name and the link. No article text and no picture is copied; every card opens the source. Stories expire after 30 days. Tagged by place (Harare, Lagos, ...) and topic. No scraping. Needs deploying. Limit: Zimbabwean fashion coverage is thin because those feeds are general news; more local sources can be added in one line each.

items.text: Fashion events from the content engine also appear in the feeds.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: stories that announce an event (a fashion week returning, a show to be hosted, tickets, pop-ups, expos, festivals, galas) appear under \"Fashion events\" with an Event tag on the Community tab. Added 28 Oct: when the title gives a day (\"opens on 12 November\", \"12-14 Nov\") the date is read and shown on the card; upcoming events come first, soonest first, and one whose day has passed is dropped. Honest limit: few publishers put a date in the title, so most events show without one (none of the events in the feeds checked on 28 Oct had a date). Not done: events in My Daily Dress Up itself (that screen is being redesigned in another session), and curator-added events merged into the same list.

tiers.name: Tier 4 — Bigger features
tiers.blurb: Clear, but large: new screens, new data, or migrations.

items.text: Bookmark categories, like Facebook's saved collections (for example "Weddings"). The same categories are used in the "look you love" picker.
items.progress: Saved looks already carry the category chosen when saving (P-3); they can now be browsed by category in Smart Wardrobe › Saved Looks and in the look picker.

items.text: "See a look you love" picker: add search plus filters for liked, bookmarked, bookmark categories, trending, style idols and people you follow. Show people you follow first.
items.progress: "Find a look you love" picker: Following (first), Fashion Twins, Saved (by category), Affirmed and Community, with search by words, category, name or @username. Still to do: Trending and Style idols sources, which need the content engine (E-2).

items.text: The Fashion Twins page currently reuses the makeover page. Rebuild it: find people (search, including the internet), add them, follow them. Their activity then appears in your feed.
items.area: Fashion Twins, Fashion Idols and Hair Stylists
items.note: Same page reused several times today
items.progress: New "My Fashion Twins" page: find people by name or @username, add them (this also asks to follow them, so their looks reach your feeds), open their profiles, remove them.

items.text: Fashion Idols works the same way: search, follow, and their news comes into your feed.
items.area: Fashion Twins, Fashion Idols and Hair Stylists
items.progress: New "My Fashion Idols" page: keep idols by name; "Style me like …" opens the makeover with the idol filled in. Still to do: idols' news and looks in the feed, which needs the fashion-content engine (E-2). Planned 25 Oct: see docs/plans/service-provider-mode.md (shopping phases). Added 28 Oct: \"In the news\" under your idols lists up to two stories that name each idol (whole name in the title). Added 28 Oct (second step): a \"From your idols\" block at the top of the Community fashion news lists up to three stories that name any of your idols, so they come to you without opening the Idols page. Not yet: looks about them (posts by or of your idol).

items.text: "My Hair Stylists" is a setup page, not a makeover page: follow stylists and salons, and keep the hairstyles you like (uploaded, found online, or your own photos).
items.area: Fashion Twins, Fashion Idols and Hair Stylists
items.progress: New "My Hair Stylists" setup page: your salons (My Circle, with "Find a salon"), "Hairstyles I like" from your photos or camera, "Try this on me" (hair makeover copying that style) and "Try a new hairstyle".

items.text: Do not add new timelines. Hairstyle makeovers and posts go into the existing My Fashion Makeover and My Daily Dress Up feeds.
items.area: Fashion Twins, Fashion Idols and Hair Stylists
items.note: Keep the number of feeds small
items.progress: The menu no longer opens the old hair flow. Its code (and the unreachable My Fashion Style page) has been deleted, about 5,400 lines; the curators' hairstyle catalogue upload moved to the admin area. Hair makeovers go through the main makeover and appear in the normal feeds. Hair looks saved in the old flow are still in the database but no longer shown.

items.text: Give every user a unique @username, separate from their display name (which does not need to be unique).
items.progress: Built: unique @username (3–20 characters; letters, numbers, dots, underscores), held in a usernames lookup so no two people can have the same one. Anyone without one is asked once, with a suggestion from their name. It shows on profiles and in search, and can be changed in Settings. Database rules deployed 20 October 2026.

items.text: Stop using email as the public identifier. Use a private ID as the key and the username for display.
items.progress: Built and tested: emails now live in a private record (owner only) and are no longer on public profiles; a full email can still be searched via a one-way hashed lookup. Every sign-in moves the email; functions/scripts/migrate_private_emails.js moves the rest. Goes live with the Friday rules deploy.

items.text: The wardrobe holds my clothes, the shops I am connected to and the designers I am connected to.
items.progress: The wardrobe's Shops & Designers tab now opens with My Circle (your salons, shops and designers, removable), then the directories.

items.text: Add item: take a photo of the piece, and the app detects the colour. Do not ask for colour by hand.
items.progress: First version built 27 Oct: choosing a photo in Add item pre-selects its colours (up to two), with the note "Picked from your photo. Tap to change." Done on the phone from the pixels, with no AI call, so it is free and instant. The middle of the photo counts more than the edges, so a garment against a plain wall comes out right. Limits: it looks at the photo before the background is removed, so a busy or coloured background can fool it; patterned clothes give their main colours only; not yet tried on real photos or a phone. The shop stock form does not have it yet.

items.text: Saved items and looks can be put into categories and are interactive. They should not feel dead.
items.progress: Partly done: saved looks are filed under categories, grouped in Saved Looks, open full screen and show when last worn. 27 Oct: each saved look now has a "move" button to change its category later, make a new one, or remove it from its category. Still missing: categories for clothes in My Clothes. The move button is tested only as a sheet, not yet on a phone.

items.text: Track wear: for example "You haven't worn this shirt in 10 months".
items.progress: Clothes in My Clothes have "I wore this today" and show "Worn 3 weeks ago" / "Not worn in 10 months" (highlighted after 6 months, or when never worn after a month). Saved Looks show when each was last worn, from "Wear today".

items.text: Shops and designers you follow add new stock that matches your profile and wardrobe to this feed ("New look from <shop>").
items.progress: All 3 steps built (1 and 2 on 26 Oct, 3 on 28 Oct). (1) Matching rules, tested: from a shop or designer you follow, in stock in your size (or the fit-check size), suiting a style you chose or filling a wardrobe gap; best three a day. (2) "New from shops you follow" cards at the top of My Daily Dress Up: picture, shop, price and the reasons ("In your size (M). Suits your Smart style"), tap to open the item, and "Not for me" to hide it for good. Nothing shows when nothing matches. The phone does the matching when the feed opens. Still to build: (3) a server job so the cards are ready before the app opens (needs your OK to deploy). Open: the style-name mapping needs your confirmation, gender is not matched, and no shop has a size chart yet, so most matches will rest on the usual size label. Not yet seen on a phone. (3) Built 28 Oct: a server job (Cloud Function matchNewStock) that runs when a shop adds stock or restocks a sold-out piece, applies the same rules for each follower (a JavaScript copy of the app's rules, tested against the same cases) and writes today's cards, so they are ready when the app opens; the app reads those first and works it out itself only when there are none. Up to 3 a day per person, best kept; \"not for me\" is remembered. Needs the function deployed and the new app build.

items.text: Any user can switch between Customer mode and Service-provider mode, like switching between passenger and driver in InDrive. One person can be both.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: a Customer / Provider switch at the top of the menu and a "Provider mode" row in Settings. Switching never signs you out. The old Seller Mode switch (which turned the whole app into the shop screen) is gone.

items.text: A provider can be a shop, a designer, a hair stylist or salon, or several of these at once.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: one person can hold shop, designer and salon together; roles set up before are carried over automatically.

items.text: Provider mode has its own screens: my shop, my designs, my salon, with forms to enter stock and services.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: a provider home with a card per role (My Shop, My Designs, My Salon), "Orders & requests" (orders, design requests and hair requests together, with Accept / Decline / Completed and a notification to the customer) and Messages. Needs the new database rules deployed for design and hair requests.

items.text: Shops and designers sign up as normal users, then switch on provider mode. No separate business sign-up.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: one "Become a provider" form (tick what you offer, business name, location) for any user; every old "Create profile" button now opens it. Listings still appear only after a curator verifies them.

items.text: Shops, including flea-market traders, upload their stock with photos, sizes, measurements and prices.
items.note: Provider mode (S) is built, so shops now reach this from My Shop.
items.progress: Partly built (the listing screen existed): photos with a back photo, sizes with stock per size, an optional size chart per size, prices, colours and style. Added 28 Oct: a proper Shoes category with UK shoe sizes (UK 3 to UK 12), which \"Get this look\" now matches against the buyer's shoe size (the wardrobe has the category too); and a stock overview on Products & Inventory: counts for all, low (2 or fewer left) and sold out, filter chips, and a colour-coded \"Only 2 left\" / \"Sold out\" on each piece. Added 4 Nov: "Quick add" on Products & Inventory for flea-market traders: a photo, a price, what kind of piece it is and the sizes in hand (UK sizes for shoes; a simple count for accessories), then "Add to my shop". Everything else gets a default and can be edited later, and after each piece the screen clears and keeps the kind so a trader can add many in a row. Also a stock button on every piece: change how many are left per size, or the single count, without opening the full form. Delivery settings were built under K-3. Not yet tried on a phone.

items.text: Electronic fitting room: try a shop's item on your own body, using your saved measurements. You can turn around and see a fit check (for example "tight around the waist"). The goal is to beat the physical fitting room.
items.note: Core value. Depends on U-6 measurements.
items.progress: Built 25 Oct (committed a641605) (first version): a "Fit check" card on clothing product pages compares the shop's garment measurements with your saved ones and says where it is tight, snug or loose ("Size M: tight around the waist"), shows the numbers, and suggests the best size in stock. Shops can enter an optional size chart (shoulders, chest, waist, hips, inseam per size) in the stock form; where there is none it compares size labels ("a size bigger than you usually wear"). The fit also goes to the Gemini try-on picture. Not yet: existing shop products have no size charts until shops add them; stretchy fabric is not accounted for.

items.text: From look to purchase: after a makeover, check whether the items are already in your wardrobe. If they are not, suggest shops that have them.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version): after a makeover, "Place Order" opens "Get this look". For each changed piece (top, bottom, clothes, shoes, accessories) it says whether you already own something like it ("You have 2 in your wardrobe" or "None in your wardrobe") and offers up to 3 pieces from verified shops that are in stock in your size, best style match first, each with one-tap "Add to bag". Hair links to hairdressers and "Have it made" to designers. It also opens from friends' looks in My Daily Dress Up (whole look). Not yet: colour matching (the look is a picture, so colour per piece is unknown); shoes are recognised by name because neither the wardrobe nor shops have a shoes category; the shop's own products only, no supplier matching.

items.text: Design the monetization module: track users, transactions, who sold what, commission and payouts.
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version): money records live in the same Supabase database as everything else (settled 22 Oct question): orders carry the commission, referrer and influencer share, and a ledger lists who owes or is owed what, by stage (pending, due, settled, void). Cancelling an order voids its entries; finishing it makes them due. Curators can mark entries settled. Each provider has an Earnings screen. Still to do: a curators' payouts screen (list who is owed, mark settled), and how commission is actually collected from shops.

items.text: Push notifications for trending looks and styles, once there are enough users to create trends.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version): every evening (18:00 Harare time) a job finds public looks affirmed by at least 3 different people in the last 24 hours and tells people in that city about the best one. At most one push a person a day, never the same look twice, never the owner or someone who already affirmed it. No counts are shown, so counts stay owner-only. A switch in Settings turns it off; tapping the notification opens the look. Stays quiet at small scale because of the 3-person rule. Needs deploying. People are matched by the city in Settings, so someone must save their city to be included.

items.text: Opt-in access to the photo gallery: suggest "Check out this look" makeovers made from the user's own photos, as Google Photos does.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version): off by default. The makeover screen offers "Start from a photo on your phone?"; turning it on shows plain-words consent (what is shown, that photos stay on the phone, that none are uploaded until you pick one, that you can turn it off). After that, your recent photos appear under "Try a makeover on a recent photo"; tapping one uploads only that photo for the makeover. Consent is stored privately and versioned (wording changes ask again); a switch in Settings withdraws it; if the phone refuses photo access it says so and points to settings. No photo is scanned, sorted or kept. Not yet tested on a real phone. Not built: choosing photos by what they show.

items.text: Turn-around (3D-style) view in the fitting room: turn the try-on around to see the sides and back.
items.progress: First version built 26 Oct: "Turn me around" on the try-on makes right side, back and left views with AI (one at a time, shown as they arrive); drag left or right, or use the arrows, to turn like a turntable. Sides and back are estimates and are labelled so. Costs three more AI image calls per try-on.  Later options: a short spin video, optional back photo from shops to improve the back view, and true 3D models once shops can supply them. 27 Oct: the angles are now kept with the saved look (also if you turn around after saving), and a saved look that has angles opens in the turn-around viewer from Saved Looks and My Daily Dress Up. Not tried on a phone yet. 27 Oct: shops can add an optional back photo for each item in the stock form; when there is one, the turn-around uses it for the back view instead of guessing. Needs a shop to add the photo, and has not been seen on a phone.

items.text: Shops and designers send a link or QR code to their stock, a category or chosen pieces: to friends, followers, the public in the app, and to many WhatsApp groups. The link lets anyone try the pieces on (eFitting) and buy them online.
items.note: Added 30 Oct at the stakeholder's request.
items.progress: Built 30 Oct (first version): "Share my stock" on the provider home. The shop picks all stock, a category or pieces, adds a title and note, and chooses who in Banigoba is told (just the link, friends, followers, or public: followers get a notification and public links show in a "From the shops" strip on Community). It then gets a link and QR code with Send on WhatsApp (WhatsApp opens with the message ready and the shop ticks the groups; WhatsApp does not let any app post to groups automatically, and limits how many chats are picked at once), other apps, the QR as a picture, and copy. Anyone opening the link sees the pieces with prices and Try on / Buy (sign-in needed for those); on a phone with the app it opens in the app. Links can be switched off. Shop products are now publicly readable (a shop window) so links work without an account; only public links can be listed. Needs: deploying the rules, the announceShopLink function and the web app (Firebase Hosting); on the web, try-on is off until image generation moves to the server, because a public web app would expose the Gemini key. Not yet: iOS universal links, opening the link again automatically after signing in, link view counts for the shop, designers' portfolio pieces (links cover shop products).

items.text: Auto-tag wardrobe items from the photo: type, colour, style, weather and gender, so nobody types them by hand.
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version): choosing a photo in Add item (wardrobe) now asks Gemini what the piece is and fills in the name, category, subcategory, style, gender, colours, weather and function tags. It only fills fields nobody has touched, only uses the app's own words (anything else is dropped), says "Filled in from your photo" and everything can be changed. Quick add (K-1) does the same for the kind and name. Not yet tried on a phone. The Gemini key is compiled into the app, as it is for makeovers; moving all Gemini calls behind a server function is a later hardening step. Season and occasion tags are not added yet.
items.note: From the client's product-design document (4 Nov 2026)

items.text: Guided first five minutes: upload a selfie, pick aesthetics, add a few wardrobe items, get an instant makeover and a first affirmation, so a new user sees value straight away.
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version): a new account now lands on a short guide instead of the single style question: four optional steps with a progress bar. (1) Add your photo (camera or gallery; it becomes the photo makeovers start from). (2) Pick your style (the existing style screen). (3) Add three pieces you own: photograph each and the AI fills in the details (W-9); they go into the private wardrobe without background removal. (4) See your first makeover (opens the makeover start). Every step can be skipped, "Skip for now" ends the guide at any time, and finishing shows a kind word from the universal affirmations (no score). It is shown once, to accounts that have not answered the style question yet; existing users are not interrupted. Not yet tried on a phone. Not in it yet: the makeover does not start automatically from the photo, and pieces do not get background removal.
items.note: From the client's product-design document (4 Nov 2026)

items.text: Wardrobe insights: how often each piece is worn, pieces never worn, near-duplicates, missing essentials and seasonal gaps.
items.progress: Built 4 Nov (first version): a "Wardrobe insights" card at the top of My Clothes opens a private page. It shows: your favourites (most worn); pieces owned over a month and never worn; pieces not worn for six months; near-duplicates (three or more of the same kind and colour, e.g. "4 blue shirts"); basics that are missing (too few tops, bottoms, shoes or outerwear, or nothing in black, white, grey or beige); and weather you are not covered for (once there are six pieces and some are tagged). It says "Only you can see this" and never compares with anyone. Not yet tried on a phone. Not in it yet: season and occasion gaps, and suggestions that link a missing basic to shops in the app (that would join this with the new-stock matching, D-4).
items.note: From the client's product-design document (4 Nov 2026)

items.text: Community pods: small groups around an aesthetic, a region or a profession, where validation is community-based rather than a global contest.
items.progress: Not started. Wait for users to ask for it.

items.text: Stylists offer virtual consultations and curated wardrobe builds, and salons take bookings in the app, with a fee per session.
items.progress: Not started. Design and hair requests and the provider inbox exist; booking, scheduling and payment do not.

items.progress: Not started. The influencer share on sales (K-6) is built in the database; recruiting agents is a separate rule to decide.

tiers.name: Tier 5 — Backend, research and go-to-market
tiers.blurb: Open-ended. Needs design or research before building.

items.text: Get the original AI and system architecture specification. Ask Da, who built the first version from it; it may also be in a ChatGPT conversation. Read it in detail.
Build the algorithms in that specification on the backend.
Community engine based on location (see the Post, save and share section).
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version): same work as P-5. Looks from people in your city rank above strangers, and the Near me view is built on the city each person chose.

items.text: Feed ranking: people you follow first, then wider.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct: the Home feeds are ranked with people you follow (and your own looks) first, then people in your city, then everyone, newest first within each group. It is a recency boost, not three separate lists: a followed author's post counts as 7 days newer, a nearby author's as 2 days newer, so a month-old post cannot bury today's. Wording of "wider" is as decided here: city first, then everyone.

items.text: Match shop and designer stock to user profiles (see the Daily Dress Up section).
items.progress: All 3 steps built (1 and 2 on 26 Oct, 3 on 28 Oct). (1) Matching rules, tested: from a shop or designer you follow, in stock in your size (or the fit-check size), suiting a style you chose or filling a wardrobe gap; best three a day. (2) "New from shops you follow" cards at the top of My Daily Dress Up: picture, shop, price and the reasons ("In your size (M). Suits your Smart style"), tap to open the item, and "Not for me" to hide it for good. Nothing shows when nothing matches. The phone does the matching when the feed opens. Still to build: (3) a server job so the cards are ready before the app opens (needs your OK to deploy). Open: the style-name mapping needs your confirmation, gender is not matched, and no shop has a size chart yet, so most matches will rest on the usual size label. Not yet seen on a phone. (3) Built 28 Oct: a server job (Cloud Function matchNewStock) that runs when a shop adds stock or restocks a sold-out piece, applies the same rules for each follower (a JavaScript copy of the app's rules, tested against the same cases) and writes today's cards, so they are ready when the app opens; the app reads those first and works it out itself only when there are none. Up to 3 a day per person, best kept; \"not for me\" is remembered. Needs the function deployed and the new app build.

items.text: Shops and smart wardrobes talk to each other: a saved look goes into the wardrobe and is matched against shop stock (see K-4).
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version, same work as K-4): a look is checked against the wardrobe and matched to verified-shop stock in your size. Added 28 Oct: shops see how far each new piece got. Products & Inventory shows \"Shown to 4 of 9 followers\" under each piece, from a count kept when the piece is matched to followers' feeds (a restock adds to it). It is a number only, readable by the shop alone; no follower is named. Needs the matchNewStock function (deployed) and the rules (not yet). Not yet: saving a look into a shop's own view.

items.text: Fashion-content engine (see E-2) and monetization tracking (see K-7).
items.progress: Content-engine half built 28 Oct (see E-2). Monetization tracking is not started (K-7).

items.text: Define "Community" (people near your location) and "Public" (anyone), and build the backend logic that decides who is in each.
items.progress: Built 28 Oct (first version): Community now has Near me / Everyone chips. "Near me" is the people you follow plus people in your city; "Everyone" is every look you may see. The city is the one a person types in Settings and is public (nothing finer is stored); without a city, the tab asks for one instead of guessing. Not yet: distance-based "near" from phone location.

items.text: Research: physical clothing tags (AirTag-style button tags, RFID) to show what is in or out of the wardrobe, what is at the wash, and to alert when an item leaves the yard (geofence). Include a way to switch a tag off while the owner wears it, and cost per tag.
Brand ambassadors: recruit influencers and pay them monthly to use the app, do makeovers, post looks and vlog about it.
Demand view for designers and shops: anonymous totals of what users are missing and what is trending in a region, so they know what to make or stock.
items.progress: Not started. Needs enough users for the totals to mean something, and must never show an individual's wardrobe.
items.note: From the client's product-design document (4 Nov 2026)

findings.text: Smart Wardrobe items are stored in a top-level user_products collection, but firestore.rules only covered users/{uid}/user_products. On the phone, My Clothes fails with PERMISSION_DENIED and new uploads are refused.
findings.action: A user_products rule was added and deployed: owners read all their items, others only public ones, and only the owner can write.

findings.text: Any signed-in user can read every post, including private and friends-only ones. The app only hides them on the phone.
findings.status: Fixed and tested; deploy with Friday's release
findings.action: Posts are readable only by their author, by followers or friends as chosen, or by anyone when public; comments follow their post. Feeds now ask only for posts the user may see. 26 rules tests pass in the local emulator (npm --prefix test_rules test). Deploying blocks the old app's feed, so it goes out with the new build.

findings.text: People search showed everyone's email address and matched partial emails, and other people's profiles showed their email.
findings.action: Emails are no longer shown, only a full email address matches, and your email appears on your own profile only (see U-3).

findings.status: Fixed and tested; deploy with Friday's release
findings.text: Any user could make themselves an admin (isAdmin / role) or mark their own shop, designer or salon profile as verified, because a catch-all rule also matched the profile record itself.
findings.action: The catch-all now only covers subcollections; users cannot set admin or verified flags on themselves. Covered by the rules tests.

findings.status: Fixed and tested; deploy with Friday's release
findings.text: The curators' "verify shop / designer / salon" buttons wrote to other users' records, which the rules never allowed, so verification could not work from the app.
findings.action: Admins may now update only the shop, designer and agent profile sections of other users.
